name: Interstitial Lung Disease in Childhood and Adulthood

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society (ATS/ERS) Classification Criteria for ILD

criteria.description: Progressive exertional dyspnea and nonproductive cough persisting for weeks to months
High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) showing reticular opacities, ground-glass opacities, or honeycombing
Restrictive ventilatory defect with reduced diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO)
Lung biopsy showing interstitial fibrosis, inflammation, or granulomatous changes consistent with ILD subtype
Exclusion of other known causes such as infection, drug toxicity, or connective tissue disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical clinical presentation plus characteristic HRCT findings and restrictive lung function impairment
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is supportive but not always required if clinical and imaging findings are definitive.

searchTerms: worsening shortness of breath with activity
weakness related to low blood oxygen

occasional.symptomName: Weight loss due to chronic illness
Arthralgia associated with connective tissue disease
searchTerms: joint pain from connective tissue disease

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension symptoms (e.g., syncope, chest pain)
searchTerms: symptoms of high lung blood pressure
fainting and chest pain from lung hypertension
shortness of breath with chest discomfort

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
Autoantibodies (ANA, RF) if associated with connective tissue disease
Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: HRCT showing reticular opacities, ground-glass opacities, honeycombing, or traction bronchiectasis
Chest X-ray with bilateral interstitial infiltrates
genetic: Mutations in surfactant protein genes (e.g., SFTPC, SFTPA2) in familial cases
Telomerase complex gene mutations (TERT, TERC) associated with familial pulmonary fibrosis
other: Restrictive pattern on pulmonary function tests with reduced DLCO
Lung biopsy demonstrating usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) or nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) patterns

distinguishingFeatures: Typically presents in older adults (>50 years)
UIP pattern predominant on HRCT and biopsy
Absence of known causes or systemic disease
History of antigen exposure (e.g., birds, mold)
ILD pattern varies with underlying disease

redFlags: Hemoptysis or acute exacerbation of ILD
references: American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society International Multidisciplinary Consensus Classification of the Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias, Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2002
